# Glasswater · CrazyGames submission sheet

## Category
Casual

## Tags (max 5)
water, survival, physics, skill, relaxing

## Description (plain text, no HTML)
You are a water strider. The skin of the pond is the only thing holding you up, and every raindrop is a meteor.

Skate across the surface and read the ripples. Every leg stroke, falling gnat and lunging fish sends real waves across the water, and waves add up when they meet in step or cancel out when they meet out of step. Tap to send out your own ring wave: time it against an incoming crest and the two erase each other, leaving a patch of glass-calm water you can stand in. Time it wrong and you make the wave bigger.

Keep feeding on the gnats and mosquitoes that fall in, but do not get so heavy that the surface lets go. Dodge raindrops, outrun the fish rising from below, stay clear of the frog at the bank, hold still when the backswimmer hunts by vibration, and route around the rainbow oil slicks that weaken the skin.

Six ponds, each a different world: a gravel puddle, a garden pond with lily pads and a koi, a rain barrel where every wave reflects, a roadside ditch with drift and passing cars, a rice paddy at night where you see only the glowing ripples, and a cold mountain tarn with hail. 150 levels with star goals, bosses at the end of every pond, an endless Storm Season after that, and six strider skeletons to unlock, each with its own feel and score multiplier. The Daily Storm gives everyone the same seven-minute weather every day.

Everything you see is the same wave simulation that decides whether you sink. What looks dangerous is dangerous.

## Controls
Mouse / touch: drag anywhere to skate. Tap (or click) to pulse a ring wave. A second finger while dragging also pulses.
Keyboard: WASD or arrow keys to skate, Space to pulse, Esc to pause.
Pulse while your ring is dark as a bright crest arrives to cancel it. Pulse while it is bright to stack waves and strike.
